section_summary: This section documents the condition and ownership of a former Teikoku Seishi textile mill, followed by U.S. and Allied policy papers on Japanese industrial capacity and reparations. The longer papers set out procedures for selecting, valuing, allocating, and transferring industrial facilities, then propose industry-specific limits for facilities and merchant shipping available for reparations.

subfiles.title: British Industrial Properties: Kobe — J. & P. Coats
subfiles.about: Lepper reports on the former Teikoku Seishi mill at Yasunaka and J. & P. Coats' interest in it.
subfiles.summary: The undamaged, operating Fuji Boseki mill employed 555 workers; its removed fine spindles could not be traced.

subfiles.title: Present Status of Teikoku Seishi Kabushiki Kaisha, Despatch No. 907
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The adviser forwards SCAP information on the former British interest in Teikoku Seishi.
subfiles.summary: Teikoku Seishi merged into Fuji Spinning in 1943. Its operating plant remains sound, and SCAP is protecting the British interest.

subfiles.title: British Industrial Properties: Kobe — J. & P. Coats
subfiles.about: A second copy of Lepper's inspection report accompanies Despatch No. 907.
subfiles.summary: The mill is intact and producing thread; the report records its machinery, workforce, and British ownership interest.

subfiles.title: Return of Tokyo Cable No. 45
subfiles.about: Lewis returns a cable and a copy of Claxton's letter for filing.
subfiles.summary: Returns Tokyo cable No. 45 and Claxton's letter to General Wickersham.

subfiles.title: Letter on Teikoku Seishi Kabushiki Kaisha
subfiles.about: Claxton relays Tokyo's account of the mill's status and protection of British interests.
subfiles.summary: Reports the 1943 merger, the mill's good condition, and SCAP's protection of J. & P. Coats' interest.

subfiles.title: Directive Transmitted to SCAP by the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.from: H. W. Moseley, State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: The committee forwards copies of Directive Serial No. 71.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Directive No. 71 for Far Eastern Commission transmission and State Department files.

subfiles.title: Assured Production Capacity Levels for Japan, Serial No. 71
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The directive establishes interim assured production capacities in eight Japanese industrial categories.
subfiles.summary: Sets retained capacity levels for machine tools, steel, thermal power, and chemicals, while denying assured levels to arsenals, aircraft, and light metals.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Directives Serial Nos. 70 and 71
subfiles.from: W. M. Cameron for J. H. Hilldring
subfiles.about: Certified copies of two SCAP directives are sent for filing.
subfiles.summary: Transmits directives on short-period controls and assured production capacities.

subfiles.title: Request for Industrial Data for FEC Negotiations
subfiles.about: Washington requests supporting data on industrial sectors under negotiation.
subfiles.summary: Requests data on power, shipping, shipbuilding, oil, automotive, chemical, explosives, and electrical industries.

subfiles.title: Approval and Transmission of SWNCC 236/35
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: The committee reports approval of its paper on reparations allocation procedures.
subfiles.summary: Requests submission to the Far Eastern Commission and advice on issuing an interim SCAP directive.

subfiles.title: Decision Amending SWNCC 236/35
subfiles.about: The secretariat identifies approved amendments and replacement pages.
subfiles.summary: Records approval, rejected proposals, and instructions to replace superseded pages.

subfiles.title: U.S. Policy on Reparations Allocations Procedures for Industrial Facilities in Japan, SWNCC 236/35
subfiles.from: Department of State; State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: The paper proposes how SCAP should select, value, allocate, and transfer Japanese industrial facilities as reparations.
subfiles.summary: It assigns SCAP final responsibility for selecting removable facilities, compiling inventories, setting consistent values, and allocating facilities within national shares. It proposes technical missions and a Reparations Technical Advisory Committee, with priorities for whole plants, useful integration, replacement of war losses, and prewar import dependence. Appendices compile earlier directives and SCAP comments; the discussion explains accounting, transfer deadlines, and limits on resale.

subfiles.title: Submission of SWNCC 236/35 to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Hilldring requests urgent consideration of the U.S. reparations allocation policy.
subfiles.summary: Requests FEC action, with an interim SCAP directive contemplated if agreement does not follow promptly.

subfiles.title: Draft Interim Directive on Advance Transfers and Reparations Allocation
subfiles.about: Hilldring asks that the enclosed draft directive be forwarded to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Seeks transmission of an interim directive on advance transfers and industrial facility allocation.

subfiles.title: Interim Directive Regarding Advance Transfers of Japanese Reparations and Reparations Allocation Procedures
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The draft prescribes advance reparations transfers and procedures for allocating industrial facilities.
subfiles.summary: Part A authorizes bounded advance deliveries to specified claimants for reconstruction, with records to offset final reparations shares. Part B gives SCAP selection, inventory, valuation, allocation, and accounting duties; it establishes claimant missions, a technical advisory committee, claim deadlines, and transfer rules.

subfiles.title: Submission of SWNCC 236/43 to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Hilldring forwards the approved policy on reparations removals for consideration.
subfiles.summary: Transmits SWNCC 236/43 conclusions on industrial facilities and merchant shipping.

subfiles.title: Approval of SWNCC 236/43
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: The committee reports approval of the reparations removals paper.
subfiles.summary: Requests that its conclusions be submitted to the Far Eastern Commission.

subfiles.title: Decision on SWNCC 236/43
subfiles.about: The secretariat records informal approval of SWNCC 236/43.
subfiles.summary: Records committee approval of the paper on industrial and shipping reparations.

subfiles.title: Reparations Removals of Industrial Facilities and Merchant Shipping from Japan, SWNCC 236/43
subfiles.doc_type: policy paper with memorandum, enclosure, and appendix
subfiles.about: The paper proposes a comprehensive U.S. position on Japanese industrial and merchant shipping reparations removals.
subfiles.summary: The Army Member urges prompt adoption of a position agreed after talks among departments and the Pauley and Strike groups. The enclosure specifies retained capacities or complete availability for claim across steel, chemicals, machine tools, power, shipbuilding, petroleum, metals, war facilities, shipping, nickel, synthetic rubber, and synthetic oil. It gives exceptions for facilities needed for fertilizer production and peaceful Japanese needs. The appendix begins to record how the agreement was reached; the paper continues beyond page 530.
